description: Homeowner installed a six-foot privacy fence along the side yard without submitting an Architectural Review Committee application. Material and stain color also deviate from approved community palette.
resolution_note: Owner submitted retroactive ARC application; fence height grandfathered after neighbor consent letters provided. Stain corrected to approved Sherwin-Williams 'Cedar Bark'.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Whitfield,

The Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee has observed the recent installation of a privacy fence at 14 Creek Valley Drive. Our records indicate no ARC application was submitted prior to construction, which is required under CC&R §3.2 governing exterior modifications. The fence height and stain color also appear to fall outside the community's approved standards.

Please submit a completed ARC application, including dimensioned drawings and a material sample, within 30 days of this notice. If the existing installation cannot be brought into conformance, the Committee will work with you on a reasonable remediation plan. No fine is being assessed at this time, and we appreciate your prompt cooperation.

The cure deadline for this matter is June 19, 2025. Please contact the management office if you have any questions or need a copy of the current architectural guidelines.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: Front lawn has exceeded eight inches in height with visible weed growth in flower beds. Multiple neighbor complaints received over a three-week period.
resolution_note: Homeowner mowed lawn and treated beds within seven days. Confirmed during drive-through inspection.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Patel,

During a routine community inspection, the Creek Valley HOA noted that the front lawn at 47 Creek Valley Drive has grown beyond the eight-inch maximum permitted under CC&R §4.1, and that weed growth is present in the front foundation beds. We understand that the recent stretch of rainy weather has made yard care difficult for many residents this month.

Please arrange to have the lawn mowed and the bedded areas weeded within 14 days of the date of this notice. The cure deadline is June 19, 2025. No fine has been assessed; this is a courtesy first notice intended to keep our shared streetscape looking its best.

If you are traveling or working with a landscape vendor on a delayed schedule, simply reply to this notice and we will be glad to note your timeline in the file.

Warm regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: A 22-foot enclosed utility trailer has been parked in the driveway for more than 72 consecutive hours, in view from the street.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Williams,

This letter serves as the third and final notice regarding the enclosed utility trailer stored in the driveway of 89 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §5.3, trailers, boats, and similar conveyances may not remain in driveways or on streets for more than 72 consecutive hours. Two prior courtesy notices were issued on June 28, 2025 and July 14, 2025 without resolution.

The Board has authorized escalation of this matter. A fine of $500 has been assessed, and additional fines of $100 per week will continue to accrue until the trailer is relocated to an approved off-site storage facility. The final cure deadline is July 16, 2025.

We would prefer to resolve this neighborly and are happy to provide a list of nearby storage yards. Please contact the management office at your earliest convenience to discuss a path forward before further enforcement action is taken.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Board of Directors

description: Rolling trash and recycling carts left at the curb for more than 24 hours after the scheduled Thursday pickup.
resolution_note: Bins returned to side yard the same evening notice was received. Homeowner noted she had been out of town.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Chen,

The Creek Valley HOA has noted that the trash and recycling carts at 23 Creek Valley Drive have remained at the curb past the 24-hour window permitted following Thursday collection. Under CC&R §4.6, carts must be returned to a side-yard or garage location not visible from the street by the end of the day following pickup.

Please return the carts to their stored location within 14 days of this notice; the cure deadline is July 26, 2025. No fine has been assessed, and we appreciate that travel, work schedules, and the summer heat can occasionally push household routines off track.

If you would like to be added to our courtesy list of homeowners who travel frequently and benefit from neighbor reminders, simply reply to this email and we will make a note.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Medium-sized dog observed off-leash on three separate occasions at the cul-de-sac near the mailbox kiosk. Witnessed by two different homeowners.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Nguyen,

The Creek Valley HOA has received multiple reports concerning a medium-sized dog observed off-leash near the cul-de-sac and mailbox kiosk adjacent to 102 Creek Valley Drive. CC&R §7.2, consistent with DeKalb County leash ordinances, requires that all dogs be on a leash no longer than six feet when outside a fenced area.

Because this is a second observation within a thirty-day period, a $50 fine has been assessed to your homeowner account. Please ensure the dog is leashed during all walks and outdoor breaks going forward. The cure deadline is May 12, 2026, and we will conduct a follow-up review of the file at that time.

We recognize how much our residents love their pets and want to keep the community safe for children, joggers, and other dogs. Please contact the management office if you would like to discuss the report or suggest a community pet-owner meeting.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Front-facing mailbox post replaced with non-conforming black wrought-iron design rather than the community-standard white cedar post specified in design guidelines.
resolution_note: Owner replaced mailbox post with approved standard within three weeks. Original wrought-iron unit donated to neighbor outside community.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Garcia,

The Creek Valley HOA noted during a routine inspection that the mailbox post at 61 Creek Valley Drive has been replaced with a black wrought-iron design. Under CC&R §3.5 and the published Architectural Design Guidelines, all front-yard mailbox posts within Creek Valley are required to be the community-standard white cedar post with black cast-aluminum box, in order to maintain a uniform streetscape.

Please arrange for replacement with the approved standard within 30 days of this notice. The cure deadline is September 7, 2025. A list of preferred vendors who carry the correct part is available from the management office at no cost to you.

We understand the existing replacement was likely installed after weather or vehicle damage to the original. Thank you in advance for your cooperation in restoring the consistent look of our neighborhood.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: A large dead pine tree leaning toward the neighboring property line poses a potential hazard during summer storms.
resolution_note: Owner contracted a licensed arborist; tree removed and stump ground on September 15, 2025. Photos on file.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. O'Brien,

During our quarterly common-area walk, the Creek Valley HOA identified a large dead pine tree at the rear of 78 Creek Valley Drive that is leaning noticeably toward the adjoining property. Under CC&R §4.3, owners are responsible for the safe maintenance of trees on their lots, particularly those that pose a foreseeable hazard during summer storm season.

Please arrange for inspection and removal by a licensed arborist within 30 days of this notice. The cure deadline is September 19, 2025. We strongly recommend obtaining at least two quotes, and the management office can share names of vendors other Creek Valley homeowners have used recently.

This notice is a courtesy and no fine has been assessed. Given the safety implications, however, we would appreciate confirmation of your removal plan at your earliest opportunity.

Respectfully,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Outdoor music and amplified speech from a backyard gathering continued past 11:00 PM on a Saturday night, generating complaints from three adjacent homeowners.
resolution_note: Homeowner apologized in writing to adjacent neighbors and confirmed party was a one-time 40th birthday event. No further incidents reported.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Thompson,

The Creek Valley HOA received three separate complaints regarding amplified music and outdoor noise emanating from 34 Creek Valley Drive on the evening of September 6, 2025, continuing past the community quiet hours that begin at 10:00 PM on weekends under CC&R §6.1.

A $75 nuisance fine has been assessed in accordance with our published fine schedule for first-time noise violations. Please ensure that future outdoor gatherings conclude amplified sound by 10:00 PM, and consider notifying adjacent neighbors in advance of events that may run late. The cure period for this matter ends on September 23, 2025.

We want Creek Valley to be a place where families celebrate milestones together, and a brief courtesy text to neighbors typically prevents complaints entirely. Please contact the office with any questions about the noise provisions.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Satellite dish mounted on front-facing roof slope, clearly visible from the primary street view, contrary to the rear- or side-mount requirement.
resolution_note: Installer returned and relocated dish to rear roof slope. Front mounting hardware removed and patched.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Hassan,

The Creek Valley HOA noted that a satellite dish has been installed on the front-facing roof slope at 56 Creek Valley Drive. While federal regulations do permit dish installation, CC&R §3.7 and the Architectural Design Guidelines require that, where signal reception allows, dishes be mounted on a rear or side-facing slope not visible from the primary street view.

Please coordinate with your provider to relocate the dish within 30 days of this notice, by October 25, 2025. Most installers will accommodate this at no additional cost when the request is made within the warranty window.

If your installer documents that no alternative location provides adequate signal, please forward that documentation to the management office and the matter will be closed without further action.

Thank you,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: A pile of bulk household items including an old mattress, two dining chairs, and cardboard boxes has been at the curb since the last regular collection day.
resolution_note: Homeowner scheduled DeKalb bulk pickup for October 9 and items removed same day.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Mitchell,

The Creek Valley HOA observed an accumulation of bulk household items, including a mattress and dining chairs, at the curb of 118 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §4.6, bulk items may be placed curbside only within 24 hours of a scheduled bulk pickup window.

Please schedule a bulk pickup through DeKalb County Sanitation, or remove the items to an alternative location, within 14 days. The cure deadline is October 17, 2025. The county currently offers a free quarterly bulk pickup; instructions for scheduling are on the management office portal.

This is a courtesy first notice and no fine has been assessed. If you would like a neighbor referral for short-distance hauling, please reach out and we will share contacts other residents have used.

Best regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Halloween inflatables and orange string lights remain installed and operating on the front lawn well past the seasonal display window.
resolution_note: Inflatables and lights taken down before Thanksgiving. Homeowner cited a broken storage bin as the delay.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Reeves,

The Creek Valley HOA has observed that Halloween-themed inflatables and seasonal string lighting remain in place at 7 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §4.4, seasonal decorations associated with a specific holiday must be removed within 14 days of that holiday's date.

We ask that the Halloween display be taken down by December 3, 2025, which represents the 14-day cure window. Standard winter holiday decorations may then be installed in accordance with the published seasonal guidelines.

This is a friendly first notice with no fine assessed; we recognize that decorations can be a substantial undertaking and that schedules slip. Please reach out if assistance with takedown would help, as our community service committee occasionally pairs volunteers with neighbors who need a hand.

Warmly,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Front door repainted bright red without architectural approval, deviating from the approved palette of muted black, navy, and forest green tones.
resolution_note: Homeowner repainted to approved Sherwin-Williams 'Iron Ore' over the holiday break. ARC approval logged retroactively.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Bennett,

The Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee has noted that the front door at 42 Creek Valley Drive has been repainted in a bright red color that is not part of the approved palette under CC&R §3.3. The approved palette is intentionally narrow to maintain the cohesive feel of the streetscape that drew many homeowners to Creek Valley initially.

Please either submit a retroactive ARC application for an alternate color within the approved palette, or repaint to one of the published options within 30 days. The cure deadline is January 1, 2026. The approved palette and color chips are available at the management office and on the homeowner portal.

No fine has been assessed. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter, and we look forward to seeing the refreshed entry.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: A commercial work van with prominently displayed signage and ladder racks has been parked in the driveway every evening for more than two weeks.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Park,

This letter is the third notice regarding the commercial work van parked nightly in the driveway of 95 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §5.2, commercial vehicles bearing exterior signage, ladder racks, or equipment may not be regularly parked in driveways visible from the street between the hours of 6:00 PM and 7:00 AM. Previous courtesy notices were issued on December 12, 2025 and January 6, 2026.

A cumulative fine of $600 has been assessed, and additional weekly fines of $150 will continue to accrue until the vehicle is consistently parked inside the garage or stored off-site overnight. The final cure deadline is February 9, 2026.

We understand the realities of a work-from-truck profession and are open to discussing a reasonable accommodation, such as garage parking or signage covers. Please contact the office to discuss before further Board action is required.

Respectfully,
Creek Valley HOA Board of Directors

description: Two unaccompanied minors used the community pool after posted closing hours of 9:00 PM, climbing the perimeter fence to gain entry.
resolution_note: Parents acknowledged incident in writing and confirmed disciplinary action with the minors. Pool access fobs reset and resident attended a brief safety conversation with the pool committee chair.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Lindstrom,

The Creek Valley HOA has reviewed a security camera incident from the evening of August 10, 2025, in which two minors registered to 71 Creek Valley Drive entered the community pool area by climbing the perimeter fence after the posted 9:00 PM closing time. Under CC&R §6.4 and the pool rules adopted by the Board, after-hours pool use is strictly prohibited due to safety and insurance considerations.

A $150 fine has been assessed to the homeowner account, consistent with the published schedule for unauthorized common-area use. The cure deadline is August 26, 2025; cure requires a written acknowledgment of the incident and assurance that the after-hours access will not recur.

We appreciate that teenagers are teenagers, and we want this resolved without lasting impact on your family. Please reach out to the pool committee chair at your convenience.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Board of Directors

description: Persistent dog waste left on the common-area greenbelt near the walking trail entrance. Observed on at least four occasions across a two-week period.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Krishnan,

The Creek Valley HOA has received multiple reports of dog waste left on the common-area greenbelt near the walking trail entrance, with sightings traced to a leashed dog walked from 29 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §7.3, residents are required to pick up after their pets in all common areas and on neighboring private property.

A $25 fine has been assessed in accordance with our published fine schedule. The cure deadline is May 18, 2026. Free waste-bag dispensers are stocked at both trail entrances; if a dispenser is empty during your walk, please notify the office and we will refill it promptly.

We are confident this is a quick fix and want our greenbelt to remain a place families and dogs enjoy together. Please contact the management office if you believe this notice has been issued in error.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: New cedar deck constructed at the rear of the home without submitted ARC application or county permit posted on site.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Williams,

The Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee has observed construction of a new cedar deck at the rear of 113 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §3.2, no exterior structural addition may commence without an approved ARC application, and DeKalb County requires that the building permit be posted on site throughout construction. Our records show no application on file.

A $100 administrative fine has been assessed, and we ask that you submit a complete ARC application including drawings, materials list, and a copy of the county permit within 30 days of this notice. The cure deadline is June 9, 2026. The application is available on the homeowner portal.

If the construction is found to meet our standards, the application can be approved retroactively and the matter closed. We appreciate your prompt cooperation so the project can continue without further delay.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: A 24-foot pleasure boat on a trailer has been parked alongside the home, partially in the side yard and partially blocking the sidewalk.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Caldwell,

The Creek Valley HOA has received complaints regarding a 24-foot pleasure boat on a trailer at 52 Creek Valley Drive. The trailer extends across the sidewalk and into the side yard, in violation of CC&R §5.3, which prohibits long-term storage of boats and recreational vehicles on residential lots, and which incorporates DeKalb County's prohibition on obstructing public pedestrian walkways.

A $75 fine has been assessed, and we ask that the boat be moved to an off-site storage facility within 14 days. The cure deadline is May 6, 2026. Several Creek Valley homeowners use the Lake Lanier and Stone Mountain marina yards, and the management office can share those references on request.

We understand boating season is just kicking off and want to help find a workable solution. Please reach out if discussion would be useful.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Front-yard zoysia turf has significant brown patches covering an estimated 40% of the visible lawn area. No remediation visible after several weeks of warm weather.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Adebayo,

The Creek Valley HOA has observed significant brown patches across the front lawn at 86 Creek Valley Drive, currently covering an estimated 40% of the visible turf. Under CC&R §4.1, owners are responsible for maintaining healthy turf in front yards, and the spring growing season is the appropriate window for remediation.

Please arrange for soil treatment, aeration, or partial resodding as needed within 30 days. The cure deadline is May 15, 2026. We recognize the past year was hard on zoysia across our area, and we are not expecting perfection; we simply need to see a credible remediation plan or visible progress.

No fine has been assessed. If lawn care has become difficult for health or schedule reasons, the management office maintains a list of vetted vendors at a community rate.

With respect,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Recycling bin overflow with cardboard breakdown visibly tossed loose alongside the cart, with materials blowing onto the neighbor's lawn.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Liu,

The Creek Valley HOA observed during this Wednesday's drive-through inspection that the recycling cart at 105 Creek Valley Drive is significantly overflowing, with broken-down cardboard placed loose alongside the cart. Material has migrated onto the adjoining lawn at 104 Creek Valley Drive during yesterday's wind. Under CC&R §4.6, all recycling must be fully contained within the cart, with the lid closed.

We ask that the loose material be collected and that future overflow be staged inside the garage until the following collection day. The cure deadline is May 28, 2026. No fine has been assessed; this is a first courtesy notice.

If household recycling volume is regularly exceeding cart capacity, DeKalb County will provide a second cart at a modest monthly fee. The management office can share the request form.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Unleashed and unregistered dog matching the breed restriction list under community insurance carrier requirements observed in the front yard repeatedly.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Mackenzie,

This letter follows three prior notices regarding the dog observed in the front yard of 67 Creek Valley Drive. The dog appears to match a breed on the restricted list maintained under our community insurance carrier's requirements, referenced in CC&R §7.4, and has been observed unleashed on multiple occasions.

A cumulative fine of $750 has been assessed. The Board has authorized escalation to legal review if compliance is not achieved by March 16, 2026. Cure requires submission of: (1) veterinary documentation of breed identification; (2) proof of homeowner's renters insurance covering the animal; and (3) confirmation that the dog is leashed in all outdoor settings.

We genuinely want to keep this matter out of legal channels. The pet committee chair would welcome a phone conversation to walk through documentation options before any further action.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Board of Directors

description: Property advertised on a short-term rental platform with weekend bookings observed via parking-lot traffic and changing license plates over several weekends.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Sutherland,

The Creek Valley HOA Board has documented evidence that 124 Creek Valley Drive has been operated as a short-term rental, with weekend listings observed on a major rental platform and corroborating vehicle turnover noted by neighbors. Under CC&R §6.5, rentals of less than thirty consecutive days are prohibited, and all leases must be registered with the management office.

A fine of $1,500 has been assessed reflecting estimated rental nights since November 2025, with additional fines of $250 per documented rental night accruing going forward. The cure deadline is February 9, 2026. Cure requires removal of all short-term listings, certification under penalty of perjury that no rentals of less than thirty days will occur, and registration of any long-term tenant.

This is a matter the Board takes very seriously due to its impact on insurance, security, and community character. We strongly encourage you to contact counsel and the management office promptly.

Respectfully,
Creek Valley HOA Board of Directors

description: Recurring late-night use of a backyard hot tub with elevated conversation volume past midnight on weeknights, drawing complaints from two adjacent households.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Hoffman,

The Creek Valley HOA has received complaints from two adjacent households regarding late-night noise from backyard hot tub use at 18 Creek Valley Drive, with conversation volume reported past midnight on weeknights. Under CC&R §6.1, exterior noise audible at the property line is restricted after 10:00 PM Sunday through Thursday and after 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.

A $50 fine has been assessed consistent with the published schedule for a first noise notice. Please observe community quiet hours going forward; the cure deadline is April 5, 2026.

We want to be clear that hot tub use is welcomed and encouraged within quiet hours. A brief conversation with adjacent neighbors often resolves these matters informally, and the office is happy to facilitate an introduction.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Christmas lights and a wire-frame reindeer remain installed on the front lawn well past the published February 1 takedown deadline for winter holiday displays.
resolution_note: Homeowner removed all winter decor by Valentine's Day. Cited an extended business trip as the cause of delay.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Nakamura,

The Creek Valley HOA has observed that winter holiday lighting and a wire-frame reindeer remain installed at 3 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §4.4 and the published seasonal display guidelines, winter holiday decorations must be fully removed by February 1 each year.

Please arrange for removal within 14 days of this notice. The cure deadline is February 19, 2026. No fine has been assessed; we recognize that February is a busy month and that wire-frame displays can be unwieldy to store.

If assistance with takedown would be helpful, our community service committee occasionally pairs volunteer help with residents who need a hand. Please reach out to the management office to coordinate.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Trash carts consistently left at curb on the wrong side of the driveway and several feet into the street, narrowing the lane on a curve.
resolution_note: Homeowner adjusted placement to the apron side of the driveway. Confirmed across three subsequent collection days.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Esposito,

The Creek Valley HOA noted during recent inspections that the trash and recycling carts at 81 Creek Valley Drive are being placed several feet into the street rather than at the driveway apron. Because 81 Creek Valley Drive sits on a curved section, the cart placement is narrowing the drivable lane and creating sight-line concerns. Under CC&R §4.6, carts should be placed at the edge of the driveway, no more than two feet into the public right-of-way.

Please adjust placement going forward; the cure deadline is November 11, 2025. No fine has been assessed.

Thank you for helping keep our streets safe. The management office can email a placement diagram if helpful.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Bulk debris from a kitchen renovation, including cabinetry, sheetrock pieces, and tile fragments, dumped at curb without contractor dumpster.
resolution_note: Contractor arranged dumpster delivery and removed all renovation debris within ten days. Homeowner provided receipt.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Hernandez,

The Creek Valley HOA observed a substantial pile of kitchen renovation debris at the curb of 99 Creek Valley Drive, including cabinetry, sheetrock, and tile. Under CC&R §4.6 and DeKalb County waste rules, construction debris may not be placed in the residential collection stream and must be staged in a contractor-provided roll-off or hauled to the transfer station.

A $100 fine has been assessed to cover administrative time and the risk of the county refusing to service the cart. Please arrange for proper removal within 14 days; the cure deadline is November 18, 2025.

Most local renovation contractors include dumpster service in their bid; we would be glad to share the names of vendors other Creek Valley homeowners have used. Best wishes on the renovation.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Window-mounted air conditioning unit installed in front-facing second-story window, visible from the street.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Foster,

The Creek Valley HOA observed during this week's inspection that a window-mounted air conditioning unit has been installed in a front-facing second-story window at 38 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §3.6, window AC units are not permitted in front- or side-facing windows visible from the street, due to consistency of streetscape and the potential for water staining on siding below.

We ask that the unit be relocated to a rear-facing window, or that an alternative cooling arrangement be made, within 30 days. The cure deadline is June 11, 2026. If a household member is using the unit due to a medical accommodation, please reach out and the office will work with you on a reasonable solution.

This is a first courtesy notice and no fine has been assessed. Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: A pop-up camper has been parked across the front of the driveway for several days, partially blocking the sidewalk.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Brennan,

The Creek Valley HOA observed that a pop-up camper has been parked across the front of the driveway at 62 Creek Valley Drive for several days, partially obstructing the public sidewalk. Under CC&R §5.3, campers and similar recreational vehicles may not remain on residential lots for more than 72 consecutive hours and may not at any time obstruct sidewalks.

Please move the camper to an off-site storage location within 14 days; the cure deadline is May 28, 2026. This is a first courtesy notice and no fine has been assessed.

If the camper is staged in advance of a planned trip, simply reply with the departure date and we will note the file. The management office is also happy to share local storage yard contacts.

Kind regards,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Glass beverage container brought into the pool deck area in violation of posted rules. Photographic evidence from pool camera retained.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Ms. Olsen,

The Creek Valley HOA pool camera captured footage from May 15, 2026 showing a glass beverage container brought into the pool deck area by a guest registered to 110 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §6.4 and the posted pool rules, glass is prohibited within the pool fence due to the safety hazard a break would create.

Please review the pool rules with all members of your household and any guests, and acknowledge receipt of this notice within 14 days. The cure deadline is May 29, 2026. This is a first courtesy notice and no fine has been assessed.

We appreciate your help keeping the pool safe and enjoyable as we move into the summer season. If you would like an extra copy of the pool rules card for your refrigerator, the office will gladly drop one off.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Compliance Committee

description: Holiday-themed window film with snowflake pattern remains on front-facing windows year-round, visible from street level.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Kim,

The Creek Valley HOA noted during a recent inspection that decorative holiday-themed window film featuring a snowflake pattern remains on the front-facing windows at 75 Creek Valley Drive. Under CC&R §3.4, decorative window treatments visible from the street must be of neutral color and consistent character year-round; seasonal patterns must be removed in line with the seasonal display guidelines.

Please remove the decorative film within 30 days; the cure deadline is June 11, 2026. This is a first courtesy notice and no fine has been assessed.

If the film also serves a privacy or solar function, the office can share examples of approved year-round options that other Creek Valley homeowners have used to good effect.

Thank you,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee

description: Solar-powered pathway lighting installed along the front walk in a bright multicolor mode, with non-matching post heights and visible cabling at the bedline.
resolution_note: Homeowner switched lights to warm-white setting, replaced the mismatched fixtures, and concealed cabling under mulch. Confirmed by ARC walk-through.
ai_draft_letter:
Dear Mr. Russo,

The Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee has reviewed the recently installed pathway lighting along the front walk at 127 Creek Valley Drive. The current configuration uses a multicolor mode with mismatched fixture heights and visible cabling, which falls outside the standards in CC&R §3.4 and the published exterior lighting guidelines.

Please switch the lights to a warm-white setting (2700K or warmer), align fixture heights, and conceal cabling within 30 days. The cure deadline is August 21, 2025. No fine has been assessed and no ARC application is needed for the corrected installation.

We appreciate the thought you've put into the front walk and just want to keep our nighttime streetscape feeling cohesive. Thank you for your prompt attention.

Sincerely,
Creek Valley HOA Architectural Review Committee
